about: What to print for each released shape. build_release.py reads this file to build the release zips, to write PRINT_LIST.md and to run --check. See README.md next to this file.

guides.title: Customize and export your own parts

items.name: Case top
items.note: Pick one. With `dpad_stick` in the name the top takes the rocker D-pad, without it the four D-pad caps. `cap_knob` or `cap_plate` is the capacitive part you print with it.

items.name: Middle plate
items.missing: The GripV view layer excludes the `case middle plate` collection, so the "Case hollow" preset skips it.

buttons.title: Button shafts
buttons.note: A shaft sits on a switch on the board and its cap clips on from above the case. All button holes are the same for now, so every button uses the one exported shaft.

items.name: Shaft for A, B, X, Y, Home and the four Select buttons
Shaft for the D-pad
items.when: with a D-pad caps top (no `dpad_stick` in its name)

caps.title: Caps
caps.note: Take the caps from the same tolerance folder as the shafts they go on: each cap is made for that shaft.

items.name: D-pad cap
items.when: with a D-pad caps top (no `dpad_stick` in its name)
items.note: The four D-pad caps are one outline turned four ways.

items.name: Select cap
items.unconfirmed: The file has four Select caps that share one preset and the export writes one of them, so the four are probably the same shape.

items.name: Capacitive knob or plate
items.note: The one your case top names: `cap_knob` or `cap_plate`.

items.name: Stick
items.note: One per side. Both stick holes are the same, so you can print one design twice or two different ones. The number is the tilt range in degrees that the stick's neck is shaped for.

sticks-GripX.title: Sticks
sticks-GripX.note: The left and right stick holes differ in size, so take one stick from each folder.

scroll-wheel-GripV.title: Scroll wheel
scroll-wheel-GripV.note: The preset copy in `blender/GripV_preset.json` does not list these three, so they may be older than the Blender file.

items.name: Wheel, wheel core and wheel holder
items.missing: The scroll wheel slot is cut for every variant, so the GripX case probably has it, but no preset exports the GripX scroll wheel. The GripV files do not match: the GripX preset has its own `scroll wheel shift X` and `scroll wheel tolerance`.

items.name: Cable holder
items.unconfirmed: It only fits a case exported with the global `cable holder` on. The export presets do not set it and the saved file has it on, so the exported cases probably have the wider USB opening for it.

items.name: Pin
items.note: One per side; each pin sits half in the top and half in the bottom.

items.name: Nut lock
items.unconfirmed: A small wedge made from the front screw settings, probably to hold a front nut in its slot, so probably one per front screw.

shapes.title: GripV standard
shapes.about: The custom ergonomic "pistol-like" shape: a solid case bottom with a thin shell top, held together with screws.
shapes.hardware: Four M2.5 DIN 912 socket-head screws with nuts hold the case together. The electronics (board, joystick modules, battery, cable) are not printed.

shapes.title: GripV hollow
shapes.about: The GripV shape as a thin shell top and bottom that clip onto a middle plate carrying the board. Lighter, and also suited to resin and powder printing.
notes: No alignment pins: the shells line up on pins of the middle plate.
shapes.hardware: The printing guide recommends the four M2.5 DIN 912 screws with nuts for now, until the middle plate is confirmed to hold the case on its own. The electronics (board, joystick modules, battery, cable) are not printed.

shapes.title: GripX xbox
shapes.about: The classic Xbox-style shape, solid, held together with screws.
shapes.hardware: Four M2.5 DIN 912 socket-head screws with nuts hold the case together. The electronics (board, joystick modules, battery, cable) are not printed.

shapes.title: GripX dualsense
shapes.about: The classic DualSense-style shape, solid, held together with screws.
shapes.hardware: Four M2.5 DIN 912 socket-head screws with nuts hold the case together. The electronics (board, joystick modules, battery, cable) are not printed.
